description: Voting Village focuses on the cybersecurity and physical security of voting machines, election infrastructure, forensic audits, ballot barcodes, and defending against election disinformation.

talks.title: Wireless Odyssey: VVSG 2.0 & Voting System Wireless Guidelines
talks.teaser: Susan Greenhalgh exposes last-minute changes to the EAC Voluntary Voting System Guidelines (VVSG 2.0) that permit wireless connectivity in voting machines.
talks.summary:
Adoption of the VVSG 2.0 Election Guidelines

In February 2021, the U.S. Election Assistance Commission (EAC) formally passed the Voluntary Voting System Guidelines (VVSG 2.0), setting national standards for voting systems.

The Last-Minute Wireless Policy Reversal

Susan Greenhalgh reveals how the finalized VVSG 2.0 draft differed drastically from public hearing versions by quietly permitting wireless components in voting machine architectures.

Evaluating the Cybersecurity Risks of Wireless Voting Devices

Greenhalgh breaks down the severe remote attack surfaces introduced when tabulators, ballot marking devices, and poll books incorporate cellular modems and Wi-Fi chips.

Advocacy for Robust Election Standards Oversight

The author calls on election officials and cybersecurity researchers to demand strict federal oversight and ban wireless interfaces from critical voting infrastructure.

talks.title: Why Hacking Voters Is Easier Than Hacking Ballots
talks.teaser: Maurice Turner explores cognitive hacking in democratic elections, showing how foreign adversaries target voter trust rather than hacking voting machines.
talks.summary:
The Shift from Hardware Exploitation to Cognitive Manipulation

While securing voting tabulators and ballot marking devices remains essential, adversaries achieve greater strategic impact by manipulating voter perceptions of election legitimacy.

Analyzing Foreign Influence Operations

Maurice Turner examines disinformation tradecraft employed by nation-state threat actors (Russia, Iran, China) to amplify polarization and erode public confidence.

The Vulnerability of Unregulated Online Information Ecosystems

Turner analyzes algorithmic amplification on social media platforms, micro-targeted advertising, and synthetic deepfakes designed to suppress voter turnout.

Building Resilience in Democratic Election Systems

The author proposes multidisciplinary defenses combining threat intelligence sharing, digital media literacy initiatives, and transparent post-election auditing.

talks.title: Voting Village Welcome Remarks
talks.teaser: Voting Village co-founder Harri Hursti welcomes in-person and virtual attendees to DEF CON 29, framing key research themes and voting machine testing labs.
talks.summary:
In this opening address at the DEF CON 29 Voting Village, co-founder and renowned election cybersecurity specialist Harri Hursti welcomes researchers, election administrators, and attendees to the village live in Las Vegas. He begins at 05:00 by recounting the historical evolution of the Voting Village and its critical role in demonstrating the security vulnerabilities present in electronic voting machines, electronic poll books, and election reporting systems.

Harri emphasizes the foundational mission of the village at 10:00, stating frankly that every machine present in the lab has exploitable weaknesses, and that future voting systems will inevitably contain flaws that require independent verification. At 15:00, he previews the hands-on lab environment, inviting participants to analyze physical ballot tabulators, voter registration equipment, and backend software platforms.

He concludes at 20:00 by highlighting the vital bridge the Voting Village builds between independent ethical hackers and local election officials. He stresses that transparent vulnerability disclosure and non-partisan technical research are indispensable to hardening election systems and safeguarding public trust in democratic institutions. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Social Media Security = Election Security
talks.teaser: Sebastian Bay investigates the commercial black market for social media manipulation, showing how cheap botnets undermine democratic election security.
talks.summary:
The Commercial Market for Online Manipulation

Digital disinformation is not limited to state intelligence agencies; a thriving global commercial market sells fake social media accounts, engagement bots, and narrative manipulation.

Mechanics of Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior

Sebastian Bay details how manipulation-service providers deploy armies of automated bot accounts to distort trending algorithms and manipulate public discourse.

Auditing Platform Moderation and Detection Evasion

Bay shares research testing the defense mechanisms of major social media platforms, demonstrating that commercial manipulation networks easily bypass bot detection.

Policy Interventions for Digital Election Security

The author calls for stricter transparency regulations on digital political advertising, coordinated threat sharing, and platform liability.

talks.title: Secrets of Social Media PsyOps
talks.teaser: BiaSciLab breaks down psychological warfare tactics on social media, analyzing how nation-state PsyOps exploit algorithmic targeting and cognitive biases.
talks.summary:
Psychological Warfare in the Digital Age

Social media platforms have transformed into active battlefields where nation-state actors wage psychological operations (PsyOps) to influence adversary civilian populations.

Deconstructing Algorithmic Amplification and Targeting

BiaSciLab explains how threat actors exploit recommendation algorithms, automated content pipelines, and emotional resonance to amplify divisive political narratives.

Micro-Targeting and Identity-Based Manipulation

The author illustrates how psychographic profiling enables adversaries to tailor weaponized disinformation to specific voter demographics and affinity groups.

Developing Cognitive Defense Mechanisms

BiaSciLab provides actionable guidelines for individuals and researchers to recognize manipulative cognitive triggers and verify digital source authenticity.

talks.title: NH SB43 Forensic Audit: Inside the Windham Election Review
talks.teaser: Harri Hursti details the forensic audit of voting tabulators in Windham, New Hampshire under SB43, explaining how mechanical ballot folds skewed scan results.
talks.summary:
Background of the Windham, NH Election Discrepancy

Following a significant vote discrepancy in the 2020 Windham, New Hampshire state representative race, the state legislature mandated a full forensic audit under Senate Bill 43.

Forensic Examination of AccuVote Optical Scan Tabulators

Harri Hursti presents the technical findings from inspecting the AccuVote-OS voting machines, analyzing firmware binaries, memory cards, and physical ballot paths.

Identifying the Root Cause: Mechanical Ballot Folds

Hursti reveals that mechanical ballot folding machines placed creases directly across candidate ovals, causing the optical sensors to register false votes when paper relaxed in storage.

Best Practices for Forensic Audits and Machine Maintenance

The author provides recommendations for rigorous post-election audit procedures, tabulator calibration, and chain of custody controls.

talks.title: EAC Keynote Remarks: Advancing Voter Access & Election Resiliency
talks.teaser: U.S. Election Assistance Commission Chairman Thomas Hicks delivers keynote remarks on voter access, federal election security funding, and defending election workers.
talks.summary:
The Role of the U.S. Election Assistance Commission

The U.S. Election Assistance Commission (EAC) serves as the primary federal agency assisting states in administering secure, accessible, and accurate elections.

Navigating the Unprecedented Challenges of the 2020 Election

Commissioner Thomas Hicks reflects on administering federal elections during a global pandemic, scaling mail-in balloting, and implementing federal cybersecurity grants.

Protecting Election Officials and Infrastructure

Hicks addresses the surge in physical threats and harassment directed at local election workers, calling for stronger federal protections and resources.

Fostering Collaboration Between Hackers and Election Administrators

The keynote emphasizes the vital role of the Voting Village and independent researchers in finding vulnerabilities before adversaries can exploit them.

talks.title: Keeping Your Information Security Policy Up to Date in Local Government
talks.teaser: Sang Oun Lee outlines how local election jurisdictions can update Information Security Policies (ISP) to protect critical municipal infrastructure.
talks.summary:
The Dual Challenge of Local Government Cybersecurity

Local municipal governments provide essential civic services across sprawling administrative networks while operating under severe budget and staffing constraints.

The Foundation of Information Security Policies (ISPs)

Sang Oun Lee explains how an up-to-date Information Security Policy establishes mandatory administrative, operational, and technical controls across government agencies.

Adapting Policies to Modern Threat Environments

Lee reviews key policy domains requiring modernization—including remote work endpoints, third-party vendor management, cloud migrations, and incident response playbooks.

A Pragmatic Implementation Framework for Municipalities

The author provides local IT and security leads with a modular framework to assess current policy posture and achieve compliance with NIST and CIS standards.

talks.title: How to Weaponize Risk-Limiting Audits to Discredit an Election
talks.teaser: Carsten Schürmann analyzes how bad-faith actors weaponize Risk-Limiting Audits (RLAs) and audit misunderstandings in election disinformation campaigns.
talks.summary:
The Promise and Assumptions of Risk-Limiting Audits

Risk-Limiting Audits (RLAs) are widely considered the gold standard of statistical election verification, designed to provide mathematical evidence that reported outcomes match paper ballots.

The Vulnerability of Audits to Weaponization

Carsten Schürmann demonstrates how nuanced statistical parameters—such as sample selection anomalies and ballot discrepancies—can be twisted by bad-faith actors to manufacture distrust.

Case Studies in Audit Exploitation

Schürmann analyzes how minor clerical discrepancies discovered during audit sampling are amplified on social media to falsely claim systemic fraud.

Designing Resilient and Transparent Audit Communications

The author provides election officials with communication strategies and public-facing audit protocols to ensure statistical transparency without fueling conspiracy theories.

talks.title: High Turnout, Wide Margins: Local Election Officials on 2020 Lessons
talks.teaser: Missouri election directors Brianna Lennon and Eric Fey share candid insights from the frontlines of administering the historic 2020 general election.
talks.summary:
The Frontline Realities of Election Administration

Local election officials in the United States operate under hyper-decentralized county structures, bearing primary responsibility for voting logistics, poll worker staffing, and tallying.

Administering Elections in a Global Pandemic

Brianna Lennon and Eric Fey discuss the massive operational pivots required in 2020—including procuring PPE, managing surges in absentee voting, and training temporary workers.

Combatting Misinformation and Sustaining Public Trust

The speakers explore the psychological toll of widespread disinformation and harassment, detailing how proactive transparency builds local voter trust.

Creating Peer Support Networks for Election Directors

Lennon and Fey highlight their podcast 'High Turnout, Wide Margins' as a collaborative forum for election administrators nationwide to exchange best practices.

talks.title: Hack the Conspiracies: A County Clerk's Defense of Election Integrity
talks.teaser: Ingham County Clerk Barb Byrum shares a powerful account of defending election workers against death threats, armed protests, and toxic conspiracy theories.
talks.summary:
The Human Toll of Post-Election Conspiracies

Following the 2020 general election, unverified fraud narratives sparked unprecedented hostility, resulting in death threats, armed protests, and harassment targeting local election workers.

Defending Election Workers and Preserving Integrity

Barb Byrum provides an eyewitness account from Michigan, detailing physical security measures enacted to protect county staff, ballot storage facilities, and canvassing boards.

Debunking Voting Machine Myths with Facts

Byrum demonstrates how hands-on public logic and accuracy testing, pre-election audits, and paper ballot trails decisively disprove claims of machine tampering.

A Call for Community and Hacker Alliances

The author urges cybersecurity researchers to partner with local clerks, advocate for election worker safety legislation, and actively counter disinformation.

talks.title: Are Barcodes on Ballots Bad? Decoding Ballot Marking Device Security
talks.teaser: Kevin Skoglund decodes 1D and 2D barcodes on ballot-marking devices (ES&S, Dominion, Unisyn), evaluating the security risks of machine-readable votes.
talks.summary:
The Proliferation of Ballot Marking Devices (BMDs)

Many U.S. election jurisdictions utilize touchscreen Ballot Marking Devices (BMDs) that print paper ballots containing both human-readable text and computer-readable barcodes.

Reverse Engineering Ballot Barcode Formats

Kevin Skoglund breaks down the proprietary 1D and 2D barcode schemas used across leading voting systems (ES&S ExpressVote, Dominion ImageCastX, and Unisyn OpenElect).

The Critical Security Flaw of Barcode Tallying

Skoglund explains that because optical scanners tally the barcode rather than the human-verified printed text, malicious malware could alter barcode data without voter detection.

Recommendations for Verifiable Paper Ballots

The author advocates for hand-marked paper ballots and optical character recognition (OCR) scanning to ensure votes counted match human intent.

talks.title: A Journalist's Perspective on Fake News & Pseudo-Events
talks.teaser: Investigative journalist Bob Sullivan explores how historical pseudo-events and digital incentives paved the way for modern election disinformation.
talks.summary:
Veteran investigative reporter Bob Sullivan provides an incisive media critique at the Voting Village, exploring the origins, structural incentives, and psychological impact of disinformation in "A Journalist's Perspective on Fake News & Pseudo-Events."

[02:48] Sullivan introduces historian Daniel Boorstin's landmark 1961 concept of the "pseudo-event"—an artificial occurrence staged purely to be reported by the press (such as press conferences, photo ops, and publicity stunts). He traces how the commercial decline of local investigative journalism combined with 24/7 cable news cycles created an information vacuum readily exploited by public relations operatives and political campaigns seeking uncritical media coverage.

[05:32] The presentation examines how the economic collapse of newsrooms and the rise of engagement-driven social media algorithms incentivized sensationalism over rigorous shoe-leather reporting. Sullivan illustrates how algorithmic amplification transforms manufactured pseudo-events into modern "fake news" [08:04], distorting public perceptions of election administration, democratic institutions, and civic reality. He concludes by urging consumers and election security practitioners to recognize pseudo-events and demand verifiable source corroboration.

talks.title: A Deep Dive on Vulnerability Disclosure in the Election Sector
talks.teaser: Tod Beardsley examines the cultural shift in election vendor vulnerability disclosure, tracing progress from adversarial hostility to coordinated CVD programs.
talks.summary:
The Evolution of Election Sector Coordinated Disclosure

Since the inaugural Voting Village at DEF CON 25, the relationship between independent security researchers and voting machine vendors has undergone dramatic transformation.

From Hostility to Structured Bug Bounties

Tod Beardsley traces how private election services providers shifted from legal threats and denial to adopting ISO-compliant Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure (CVD) policies.

Navigating Legal and Operational Vulnerability Pipelines

Beardsley analyzes the role of the CISA Vulnerability Disclosure Policy (VDP) and third-party coordination platforms in mediating voting machine CVE disclosures.

Institutionalizing Independent Security Auditing

The presentation provides recommendations for embedding continuous vulnerability research and bug bounty programs into state procurement contracts.
